However, `/dev/null` is explicitly excluded only conceptually — the code skips it because `/dev/null` does not start with `--- a/` or `+++ b/`. The `hunks` property strips `b/` from the `+++` name but handles the case where the name does not start with `b/` by setting `current = None`, silently producing no entry for that file. The only realistic non-`b/` value on the `+++` side is `/dev/null`, which is the right thing to skip. But `hunks` keys on the `+++` name only, and a deleted file has `+++ /dev/null`, so it gets no entry in `hunks`. `_outside_every_hunk` then hits `not spans` (empty or missing) and returns `False`, meaning the line is accepted without checking.
